title: Machine Behavior in Relational Moral Dilemmas: Moral Rightness, Predicted Human Behavior, and Model Decisions

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model outputs across three distinct evaluative perspectives (prescriptive moral rightness, predicted human behavior, and autonomous model decision) to measure the systematic gap between the model's idealized, normative judgments and its descriptive predictions of human behavior.

Systematically modulating the relational closeness (ranging from stranger to family member) between the observer and the wrongdoer in the Whistleblower's Dilemma to evaluate how interpersonal relationships influence the model's reporting decisions.

Analyzing model rationales using the Moral Foundations Dictionary to identify a systematic down-weighting of 'Loyalty' in favor of 'Fairness', demonstrating a culturally selective alignment that prioritizes Western universalist principles over context-specific relational duties found in collectivist cultures.
